newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, shrug off Bre-X woes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, shrug off Bre-X woes.

text.p: NY precious metals ended weaker ahead of the Easter long weekend holiday, shedding gains from Thursday's shortcovering rally and failing to draw much strength from the weakness in equities and the dollar, and shrugging off Bre-X's woes, traders said.
"Monday is first notice day in the gold and we had some booksquaring ahead of that. The rollover and spread trading accounted for the bulk of activity," Tim Porter of Refco said.
June COMEX gold settled $1.00 lower at $352.50 an ounce, off the day's low of $351.50 and ending the week comfortably above the key psychological level of $350.00 an ounce.
Dealers were anxious to tidy up their positions because the London market will be closed on Monday.
COMEX and NYMEX are shut Friday for Easter holiday, along with London.

Early in the session floor sources said traders were a little leery following Wednesday's shortcovering rally in the market, partly fueled by the doubts looming over the extent of Bre-X's gold reserves.
But Greg Drury of Mitsui and Co, USA said although gold equities were "being murdered" by the fallout from Bre-X's woes, yellow metal prices were no longer being influenced.
"On the actual gold spot market, I don't think Bre-X is making any difference at all," Drury said.
The Philadelphia gold shares (XAU) index was down 5.09 points late afternoon to 105.10, hit by the double whammy of Bre-X's woes and the wider, post interest rate hike slide on Wall Street.
But some dealers were puzzled that gold did not draw much support from a three percent drop in the Dow Industrials and a weaker dollar.
"If we get a few more days in the stock market like today, then it should lend support to the gold market," Drury added.
COMEX May silver went out 1.8 cents weaker at $5.124 an ounce, traded $5.18 to $5.12 - well away from the key support level of $5.10 tested earlier this week.
Volume in gold and silver were estimated at a modest 48,000 and 16,000 lots respectively.
Dealers still see the gold market as being fundamentally undecided about which way to go, with many players adopting a neutral stance for the time being.
The white metals also ended weaker, with NYMEX April platinum down $3.60 at $373.60 an ounce, traded $376.00 to $373.00.
June NYMEX palladium went out $1.20 weaker at $148.20 an ounce.
